theory.intro: A logarithmic equation has the unknown inside a logarithm; an exponential equation has it in the index. Both are solved by moving to the other form. For $\log_{a}x=k$, rewrite in index form as $x=a^{k}$; for $\log_{x}a=k$, rewrite as $x^{k}=a$ and undo the power. For $a^{x}=b$, if both sides can be written to the same base the indices must be equal; if not, take the logarithm of both sides and make $x$ the subject. Since a calculator has a base-$10$ logarithm button, the change-of-base rule $\log_{a}b=\dfrac{\log_{10}b}{\log_{10}a}$ turns any such answer into a number.
facts: $\log_{a}x=k$ means $x=a^{k}$ — read the base to the power of the number the log equals.
$\log_{x}a=k$ means $x^{k}=a$, so $x=\sqrt[k]{a}$; only the positive base is allowed.
A negative or fractional $k$ is valid: $\log_{a}x=-2$ gives $x=a^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{a^{2}}$.
If $a^{m}=a^{n}$ (with $a>0$, $a\ne1$) then $m=n$: rewrite $243$ as $3^{5}$ and $\dfrac{1}{512}$ as $2^{-9}$ to read the index off directly.
When the sides cannot share a base, take $\log_{10}$ of both sides, then $\log_{10}a^{x}=x\log_{10}a$ brings the index down as a factor.
For $k\times a^{x}=b$, divide by $k$ to isolate $a^{x}$ **before** taking logarithms.
In a model such as $FV=PV(1+r)^{n}$, substitute the known values, divide to isolate the power, then take logarithms to solve for the exponent $n$.
$a^{x}=b$ with $b\le0$ has no solution, because a positive base raised to any index stays positive.
Keep the full value in the calculator and round once, to the accuracy the question pins.
steps: Rewrite a logarithmic equation in index form, or write both sides of an exponential equation to a common base if possible.
If a coefficient multiplies the power, divide to isolate the exponential term.
Take $\log_{10}$ of both sides and use $\log_{10}a^{x}=x\log_{10}a$ to bring the index down.
Make the unknown the subject and evaluate, rounding as the question asks.

development.question_text: An investment of $\$20\,000$ grows at $6\%$ p.a., so its value after $n$ years is $FV=20\,000(1.06)^{n}$. Find the number of years for it to reach $\$50\,000$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

mastery.question_text: A car bought for $\$300\,000$ loses $8\%$ of its value each year, so its value after $n$ years is $S=300\,000(0.92)^{n}$. Find how long it takes to fall to half its original value, correct to the nearest $0.1$ years.
An investment of $\$5\,000$ grows at $8\%$ p.a., so its value after $n$ years is $FV=5\,000(1.08)^{n}$. Find how long it takes to reach $\$20\,000$, correct to the nearest $0.1$ years.
